title.narrative: Danish Multilateral Contribution to WFP Relief Operations

description.narrative: WFP is the UN's largest humanitarian organisation. Its mission is to save lives and end hunger. In 2018 WFP distributed food to more than 80 million people in 75 countries. More than 80 per cent was directed to vulnerable groups such as women and children, mapped and targeted by WFP. WFP is consolidating its strategic shift from traditional food aid to strategic food assistance with focus on nutrition and fortified foods as well as the use of innovative tools, such as cash and vouchers, e-cards and forward purchase mechanisms which includes local and regional procurement. WFP seeks to facilitate market and product development locally, while reducing market distorting effects of traditional food aid. Denmark primarily supports WFP's emergency efforts, which represent over 80 per cent of WFP's programme of work and budget. The bulk of WFP's operations take place in Africa, as well as in a number of acute and emerging crisis (in 2018 with a focus on Yemen, Iraq, Syria, South Sudan and the Central African Republic). WFP plays a central role in the provision of emergency logistics, latest under the Ebola outbreak in Congo DRC, including air services and telecommunications on behalf of the entire UN system through the global cluster system, as well as co-leading the global cluster on food security with FAO. WFP fundraised 7,4 billion USD with a budget gap of approx. 30 %. In 2018 Denmark was the 18th largest bilateral donor with a contribution of 203 mio. DKK un-earmarked. and a record high level of earmarked contributions directed to WFP's relief operations in particular in Syria and affected countries,In addition, Denmark provides stand-by partners to WFP as well as support through the Junior Professional Officer programme.
